title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
summary: Everything around you is made of matter. Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.

sections.heading: Three States of Matter
sections.text: Everything around you is made of matter. Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas. A solid keeps its own shape. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. A gas spreads out to fill all the space it can.

sections.heading: Heating and Cooling
sections.text: Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to another. When ice is heated it melts into liquid water. When water is heated more it boils and turns into a gas called water vapour. When water vapour cools it condenses back into liquid drops.

sections.heading: Tiny Particles
sections.text: Matter is made of tiny particles. In a solid, the particles are packed tightly and only wiggle in place. In a liquid, they are close together but slide past each other. In a gas, the particles are far apart and zoom around quickly.
